questions.question: In which state of India are the three crops of rice — called ‘aus,’ ‘aman,’ and ‘boro’ — grown?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, particularly in states like **West Bengal**, **Assam**, and **Odisha**, the prevailing climatic conditions allow for the cultivation of three distinct crops of rice within a single agricultural year.
 
• The three varieties are identified based on their seasonal cycles and are locally named **Aus**, **Aman**, and **Boro**.
 
• **Aman** is the primary **winter rice** crop. It is typically sown during the onset of the **Southwest Monsoon** in June and July and harvested between November and December. It occupies the largest portion of the total rice area in the state.
 
• **Aus** is referred to as **autumn rice**. It is sown during the pre-monsoon period in May and June and harvested in the autumn months of September and October.
 
• **Boro** is known as **summer rice**. This variety is sown in the winter (November to January) and harvested in the summer (April to May). Its cultivation is heavily reliant on **assured irrigation** facilities during the dry season.
 
• The **fertile alluvial soil** and the hot, humid climate of the **lower Gangetic plains** in **West Bengal** provide the ideal environment for this intensive cropping pattern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice (Oryza sativa)**:

 
 
• It is the **staple food crop** for a significant majority of India’s population and is primarily a **Kharif crop**.
 
• Growth requires high temperatures (above **25°C**), high humidity, and annual rainfall exceeding **100 cm**.
 
• **West Bengal** is consistently among the top producers of rice in India, contributing significantly to the national **food security**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context of Other Options**:
 
 
• In **Manipur** and **Nagaland**, rice is often grown using **Jhum (shifting) cultivation** or **terrace farming** in hilly terrains, where a single crop is more common due to topographical constraints.
 
• While **Bihar** is a major rice producer, the specific nomenclature and systematic triple-cropping of **Aus, Aman, and Boro** are most traditionally associated with the **Bengal delta** region.

questions.question: Which national statistical organization is being changed by the Indian government's September 2025 draft bill ahead of its centenary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** has introduced a draft bill to amend the **Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959**, aiming to modernize the governance and administrative framework of the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**.
 
• The **Indian Statistical Institute** was established by the legendary statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** on **December 17, 1931**, and was later declared an **Institution of National Importance** by an Act of Parliament in **1959**.
 
• As the institute approaches its **centenary** year in **2031**, the government seeks to restructure its organizational hierarchy to enhance efficiency and accountability in its academic and research pursuits.
 
• A significant proposal in the draft bill includes the redesignation of the head of the institute from **Director** to **Director General**, bringing it in line with the leadership structure of other elite scientific and research organizations in **India**.
 
• The proposed legislation also focuses on reforming the **ISI Council**, which is the apex governing body, to improve the decision-making process and integrate modern management practices within the premier statistical body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** and **Central Statistics Office (CSO)**:

 
 
• The **NSSO** was previously responsible for conducting large-scale nationwide sample surveys on various socio-economic aspects.
 
• The **CSO** was the nodal agency for coordinating statistical activities and preparing **National Accounts**, including **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** estimates.
 
• In **May 2019**, the **Government of India** merged the **NSSO** and the **CSO** to form a unified **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the **MoSPI**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**:
 
 
• This ministry consists of two wings: the **Statistics Wing** (NSO) and the **Programme Implementation Wing**.
 
• It is responsible for the release of key economic indicators such as the **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** and the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**.
 
• The ministry also monitors the progress of **Central Sector Projects** costing 150 crore rupees and above.

questions.question: Which of the following Union Territories of India was granted legislature through the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963** was enacted by the Parliament to provide for **Legislative Assemblies** and **Councils of Ministers** for certain Union Territories (UTs).
 
• This Act was a direct consequence of the **14th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962**, which introduced **Article 239A** to the Indian Constitution, allowing Parliament to create a local legislature for UTs.
 
• **Puducherry** (then Pondicherry) was officially granted its own legislature through this Act in **1963**, shortly after its **de jure** transfer from **French** administration to India.
 
• The **Legislative Assembly of Puducherry** consists of **30 members** chosen by direct election and up to **3 members** nominated by the Central Government.
 
• Initially, the Act also provided legislatures for **Himachal Pradesh**, **Manipur**, **Tripura**, and **Goa, Daman and Diu**, though most of these territories eventually achieved full **statehood**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi**:

 
 
• While it has a legislature, it was not established by the 1963 Act. It was granted a **Legislative Assembly** through the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991** and **Article 239AA**.
 
• The **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991** provides the legal framework for its governance.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh**:
 
 
• Created as a Union Territory in **1966** via the **Punjab Reorganisation Act** to serve as a shared capital.
 
• It is governed by an **Administrator** and does not have its own **legislature** or **Council of Ministers**.
 
 
 
• **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**:
 
 
• Established as a Union Territory in **1956**, it is administered directly by the **President** through a **Lieutenant Governor**.
 
• It remains a UT without a **Legislative Assembly**.

questions.question: Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was the capital of which empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayanagara Empire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hampi**, situated on the southern bank of the **Tungabhadra River** in the state of **Karnataka**, served as the magnificent capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** from **1336 to 1565 AD**.
 
• The empire was founded by two brothers, **Harihara I** and **Bukka Raya I**, belonging to the **Sangama Dynasty**, who established a stronghold against the expansion of the northern Sultanates.
 
• The city reached its cultural and territorial peak during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya** (1509–1529 AD), who is considered the most powerful ruler of the **Tuluva Dynasty**.
 
• **Hampi** was renowned globally for its architectural brilliance, featuring massive fortifications, complex **Dravidian-style** temples, and innovative urban planning including aqueducts and markets.
 
• The prosperity of the city came to a violent end in **1565** following the **Battle of Talikota**, where a coalition of **Deccan Sultanates** (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, and Bidar) defeated and subsequently plundered the capital.
 
• In recognition of its historical and architectural significance, **UNESCO** designated the group of monuments at **Hampi** as a **World Heritage Site** in **1986**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire**:

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Golden Age of India** (4th to 6th century CE), its primary capital was located at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna).
 
• Known for advancements in **Sanskrit literature**, **astronomy**, and the **decimal system**.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire**:
 
 
• An empire of Central Asian origin established by **Babur** in **1526**.
 
• The empire’s prominent capitals included **Agra**, **Fatehpur Sikri**, and **Shahjahanabad** (Old Delhi).
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire**:
 
 
• Founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** in **322 BCE**, it was the first pan-Indian empire.
 
• Its administrative center and capital was **Pataliputra**, and it is most famous for the reign of **Ashoka the Great**.
 
 
 
• **Virupaksha Temple**:
 
 
• One of the oldest structures in **Hampi**, dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, which remained an active place of worship even after the city was abandoned.

questions.question: Which mode of transport is most suitable for transporting heavy, bulky goods over long distances in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Railways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Railways** serve as the principal mode of transportation for freight in India, particularly for **heavy and bulky goods** over long distances, due to their immense load-bearing capacity and cost-efficiency.
 
• The **Indian Railways** network is one of the largest in the world, spanning over **68,000 kilometers**, which allows for the seamless movement of materials between mineral-rich zones and industrial hubs.
 
• Bulk commodities like **coal**, **iron ore**, **cement**, **food grains**, and **fertilizers** constitute the majority of the freight traffic, as rail transport can carry massive volumes in a single trip compared to other modes.
 
• From a technical perspective, a single freight train can carry a load equivalent to approximately **70 to 100 trucks**, making it far more **energy-efficient** and reducing the **logistics cost** per tonne-kilometer for the national economy.
 
• The development of **Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC)**, such as the **Eastern** and **Western DFCs**, has been specifically designed to increase the speed and efficiency of heavy goods movement across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waterways**:

 
 
• While scientifically the cheapest mode of transport, **Inland Waterways** in India are limited by the navigability of rivers and seasonal water levels, currently carrying a much smaller share of bulk freight compared to rail.
 
 
 
• **Roadways**:
 
 
• Best suited for **short to medium distances** and providing **door-to-door service**, but they become economically unviable for extremely heavy bulk goods over long stretches due to high fuel consumption.
 
 
 
• **Airways**:
 
 
• The most expensive mode, utilized primarily for **perishable goods**, high-value electronics, or emergency supplies, and is unsuitable for heavy industrial raw materials.

questions.question: The inscriptions of Ashoka and Kharavela were primarily written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashokan Inscriptions**: The majority of the edicts issued by the **Mauryan Emperor Ashoka** (reigned c. **268−232 BCE**) were composed in **Prakrit**. These inscriptions were strategically placed across the Indian subcontinent to propagate his philosophy of **Dhamma** in the vernacular language of the common people.
 
• **Hathigumpha Inscription**: King **Kharavela** of the **Chedi Dynasty** (Mahameghavahana) of **Kalinga** inscribed his achievements in the **Hathigumpha Inscription** at **Udayagiri**, Odisha. This 17-line record is written in **Prakrit** using the **Brahmi script**.
 
• **Language vs. Script**: It is essential to note that while the language was **Prakrit**, the scripts varied. Most inscriptions used **Brahmi**, but in the northwestern regions, **Kharoshthi**, **Greek**, and **Aramaic** were also employed to reach local populations.
 
• **Administrative Use**: During the **3rd and 2nd centuries BCE**, **Prakrit** served as the primary language for royal proclamations and administrative records, preceding the dominance of **Classical Sanskrit** in later centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pali**

 
 
• Commonly associated with the **Theravada Buddhist** canon and the **Tipitaka**.
 
• While linguistically related to Prakrit, it was not the formal language used in the **Ashokan** or **Kharavela** inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit**
 
 
• The use of **Sanskrit** in royal inscriptions became prominent later, notably with the **Junagadh Rock Inscription** of **Rudradaman I** around **150 CE**.
 
• It eventually became the court language during the **Gupta Empire**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Writing**
 
 
• The **Brahmi script** used in these Prakrit inscriptions is the ancestor of most modern Indian scripts, including **Devanagari**, **Bengali**, and **Tamil**.

questions.question: What does PCB stand for in a Computer System?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Printed Circuit Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Printed Circuit Board (PCB)** is a rigid structure that physically supports and electrically connects **electronic components** using conductive pathways, tracks, or signal traces etched from **copper** sheets.
 
• In the context of a **Computer System**, the most significant PCB is the **Motherboard** (also known as the mainboard or system board), which serves as the backbone for connecting the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Random Access Memory (RAM)**, and all other internal hardware.
 
• PCBs are typically manufactured using a **non-conductive substrate** material, most frequently **FR-4**, which is a flame-retardant fiberglass-reinforced epoxy laminate.
 
• The primary function of a PCB is to ensure a stable **electrical connection** between components like **transistors**, **capacitors**, and **microprocessors**, while providing a compact and reliable layout for complex circuitry.
 
• The production of PCBs involves a process called **photolithography** or **chemical etching** to remove unwanted copper, leaving only the required circuit traces that define the **electronic architecture** of the device.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Layers of a PCB**:

 
 
• **Solder Mask**: The outermost layer (typically green) that protects the **copper traces** from oxidation and prevents **solder bridges** during component assembly.
 
• **Silkscreen**: A layer of **ink traces** used to print labels, component identifiers (reference designators), and logos for easier maintenance and repair.
 
 
 
• **Process Control Block**:
 
 
• In the domain of **Operating Systems** (software), the acronym **PCB** can also refer to a **Process Control Block**, which is a data structure used by the **Kernel** to store information about a specific **active process**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Circuitry**:
 
 
• Before PCBs, circuits were built using **point-to-point wiring**, which was highly susceptible to **short circuits** and mechanical failure as complexity increased. The transition to PCBs allowed for the **miniaturization** of modern laptops, smartphones, and high-performance servers.

questions.question: Select the correct formula of Aluminium Sulphate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al₂(SO₄)₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical formula of **Aluminium Sulphate** is determined using the **valency** or **oxidation state** of the constituent ions to ensure the resulting compound is **electrically neutral**.
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** is a group 13 element and typically forms a cation with a charge of **+3** (**Al³⁺**), meaning it loses three electrons to achieve a stable octet.
 
• The **Sulphate ion (SO₄)** is a polyatomic anion consisting of one sulphur atom and four oxygen atoms, carrying a collective charge of **-2** (**SO₄²−**).
 
• Applying the **criss-cross method**, the numerical value of the charge of the **Aluminium ion** (3) becomes the **subscript** for the **Sulphate ion**, and the numerical value of the charge of the **Sulphate ion** (2) becomes the **subscript** for the **Aluminium ion**.
 
• To balance the total charge: **2 × (+3) + 3 × (−2) = 0**. Therefore, two aluminium atoms combine with three sulphate groups to form **Al₂(SO₄)₃**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties and Characteristics**:

 
 
• **Molar Mass**: The anhydrous form of **Aluminium Sulphate** has a molar mass of approximately **342.15 g/mol**.
 
• **Physical Appearance**: It usually appears as a **white crystalline solid** or powder and is highly **hygroscopic**, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the air.
 
• **Solubility**: It is **highly soluble in water** but virtually insoluble in **ethanol**. When dissolved in water, it undergoes hydrolysis to form an **acidic solution**.
 
• **Industrial Uses**:
 
 
• **Water Purification**: It acts as a **coagulant**, causing impurities to clump together (flocculation) so they can be easily filtered out.
 
• **Paper Industry**: Used as a **sizing agent** to adjust the paper's absorbency and improve its printability.
 
• **Textile Dyeing**: Functions as a **mordant**, helping dyes adhere to fabric fibers like cotton.

questions.question: In which year was the Planning Commission, later renamed as NITI Aayog, established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Planning Commission** of India was established on **15 March 1950** through an executive resolution of the **Government of India**.
 
• It was created based on the recommendations of the **Advisory Planning Board**, which was constituted in **1946** under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• The organization functioned as an **extra-constitutional** and **non-statutory** body, meaning its existence was not defined by the **Constitution of India** nor created by an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** of India served as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the commission; **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru** was its first chairman, while **Gulzarilal Nanda** served as the first **Deputy Chairman**.
 
• Its primary mandate was to formulate **Five-Year Plans** to promote the balanced and effective utilization of the country's resources for economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**

 
 
• Established on **1 January 2015**, it replaced the **Planning Commission** to better serve the needs of a modern India.
 
• It serves as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Union Government, providing both directional and policy inputs.
 
• Unlike the Planning Commission which followed a **top-down approach**, NITI Aayog emphasizes a **bottom-up approach** and the spirit of **Cooperative Federalism**.
 
 
 
• **National Development Council (NDC):**
 
 
• Formed on **6 August 1952**, the NDC was the apex body responsible for the final approval of the **Five-Year Plans** prepared by the Planning Commission.
 
 
 
• **The First Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• Launched in **1951** (covering the period **1951−1956**), it was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** and focused primarily on the development of the **agricultural sector**.

questions.question: Which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act has inserted the word ‘socialist’ into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, enacted in **1976** during the **Internal Emergency** under the **Indira Gandhi** administration, is the most extensive amendment in the history of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• This amendment is famously known as the **Mini-Constitution** because it introduced massive changes to the **constitutional structure**, including the **Preamble**, **Fundamental Rights**, and **Directive Principles**.
 
• For the first and only time since the adoption of the Constitution, the **Preamble** was amended to include three new terms: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• The insertion of the word **Socialist** was intended to emphasize the **egalitarian** goals of the Indian state, specifically **Democratic Socialism**, which aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease, and inequality of opportunity.
 
• The addition of **Socialist** formally aligned the **Preamble** with the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, particularly **Article 39**, which seeks the equitable distribution of material resources.
 
• Unlike the **communistic socialism** of the Soviet model, **Indian Socialism** is a **Gandhian-Marxist** blend that favors a **mixed economy** where the private and public sectors co-exist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **38th Constitutional Amendment Act (1975)**:

 
 
• Empowered the **President** to declare a state of **Emergency** that would be non-justiciable in a court of law.
 
• Ensured that **Ordinances** promulgated by the President or Governors could not be challenged in court.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978)**:
 
 
• Enacted by the **Janata Government** to undo several controversial changes brought by the **42nd Amendment**.
 
• It removed the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights** and made it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002)**:
 
 
• Inserted **Article 21A**, making **Free and Compulsory Education** a Fundamental Right for children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• Added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents and guardians.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct match of a climate type with its vegetation or features as per Koeppen's scheme of classification of climate?

options.text: Aw – Deciduous forests and tree-shredded grasslands

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aw - Deciduous forests and tree-shredded grasslands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BWh** represents the **Subtropical Hot Desert climate**. The letter **B** stands for arid climates, **W** for desert (Wüste), and **h** for hot. This climate is characterized by high temperatures and extremely low precipitation, supporting **xerophytic vegetation** like cacti and thorny bushes rather than a **dense evergreen canopy**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• **ET** stands for the **Tundra climate** within the **Polar (E)** group. In this climate, the average temperature of the warmest month is between **0°C** and **10°C**. The vegetation consists of **mosses, lichens, and stunted shrubs**, while **tropical rainforests** are associated with the **Af** climate. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• **Aw** denotes the **Tropical Savanna climate**. It is defined by a distinct **dry season** (usually in winter) and a wet season. questions.question: Frequencies higher than the human audible limit of 20,000 Hz are classified as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultrasound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human auditory system is sensitive to a specific range of vibrations known as the **audible range**, which typically spans from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• Sound waves with frequencies that surpass the upper limit of **20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**) are scientifically classified as **ultrasound** or **ultrasonic waves**.
 
• While these waves are physically identical to audible sound in terms of propagation, they are **inaudible** to the human ear because the **tympanic membrane** cannot vibrate at such high speeds.
 
• Many animals, including **bats**, **dolphins**, and **porpoises**, have the biological capability to produce and hear ultrasound, utilizing it for **echolocation** to hunt and navigate.
 
• The **Hertz (Hz)** is the standard **SI unit** of frequency, representing the number of **cycles per second**; thus, ultrasound involves over 20,000 vibrations every second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasound**:

 
 
• Refers to sound waves with a frequency **below 20 Hz**, which is the lower limit of human hearing.
 
• Sources include **seismic waves** from earthquakes, **volcanic eruptions**, and **ocean tides**.
 
• Large mammals like **elephants** and **rhinoceroses** communicate using infrasonic signals over vast distances.
 
 
 
• **Supersonic**:
 
 
• This term describes the **velocity** of an object rather than its frequency. An object is supersonic if it travels faster than the **speed of sound** (approximately **343 m/s** in air).
 
• When an aircraft reaches supersonic speeds, it produces a **sonic boom** due to the accumulation of shock waves.
 
 
 
• **Tones**:
 
 
• A **tone** is a sound that consists of a **single, pure frequency**. Most musical sounds are actually "notes," which combine a fundamental frequency with several **harmonics**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of Ultrasound**:
 
 
• **Medical Imaging**: Utilized in **sonography** to visualize fetuses and internal organs without ionizing radiation.
 
• **SONAR**: Used by submarines and ships to detect **underwater obstacles** and measure the **depth of the sea**.
 
• **Industrial Cleaning**: High-frequency vibrations are used to remove contaminants from delicate **electronic components** and surgical instruments.

• **Accountability:** They incorporate the **'Polluter Pays'** principle, holding the responsible party liable for the costs of restoration.
 
• **Thresholds:** Sites are declared 'contaminated' if hazardous substance concentrations exceed the **response levels** specified in the rules.

Important Provisions:__

• A **centralized online portal** is used to maintain an inventory of suspected, probable, and confirmed contaminated sites.
 
• Exclusions include sites affected strictly by **radioactive waste**, **mining operations**, or **marine oil spills**, which are governed by other specific acts unless contaminants exceed the response levels defined in these new rules.

Final Answer: The rules that define the process of identification, determination, and remediation of contaminated sites are the **Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025**.

questions.question: Which pollutant from the following is mainly responsible for the formation of acid rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid rain** refers to any form of precipitation, including rain, snow, or fog, that contains elevated levels of **nitric** and **sulphuric acids**.
 
• The primary chemical responsible for this phenomenon is **Sulphur dioxide (SO₂)**, which is released into the atmosphere through the **combustion of fossil fuels** (like coal and oil) in **power plants** and industrial boilers.
 
• Once in the atmosphere, **SO₂** reacts with **water vapor**, **oxygen**, and other chemicals to form **Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄)**, which eventually falls to the ground as acid rain.
 
• While normal rainwater is slightly acidic with a **pH value** of about 5.6 (due to dissolved **Carbon dioxide**), acid rain typically has a **pH value** between 4.2 and 4.4.
 
• The environmental impact of acid rain includes the **acidification of aquatic environments**, damage to **forest vegetation**, and the **chemical weathering** of stone buildings and cultural monuments like the **Taj Mahal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon monoxide (CO)**:

 
 
• A colorless, odorless, and highly toxic gas produced by the **incomplete combustion** of carbon-based fuels.
 
• It does not directly contribute to acid rain but poses significant health risks by reducing the **oxygen-carrying capacity** of blood.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃)**:
 
 
• Found in the **troposphere**, it acts as a **secondary pollutant** and a major component of **photochemical smog**.
 
• While it helps catalyze some atmospheric oxidation processes, it is not a direct precursor to acid rain formation.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃)**:
 
 
• An **alkaline gas** primarily emitted from **agricultural activities**, livestock management, and fertilizer use.

questions.question: Tholpavakoothu, the traditional shadow puppetry performance, originates from which Indian state?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tholpavakoothu** is a traditional ritualistic **shadow puppetry** art form that originated and is primarily practiced in the state of **Kerala**, specifically in the districts of **Palakkad**, **Thrissur**, and **Malappuram**.
 
• The name is a compound of three Malayalam words: **Thol** meaning leather, **Pava** meaning puppet, and **Koothu** meaning play or performance.
 
• It is traditionally performed in specially constructed permanent theaters called **Koothumadams** located within the premises of **Bhadrakali** temples, as an offering to the goddess.
 
• The performance is based on the **Kamba Ramayana**, the Tamil version of the epic written by the poet **Kambar**, spanning across 21 parts over 21 nights.
 
• The puppets are crafted from **deer skin**, meticulously perforated to create intricate patterns that project shadows onto a white cloth screen when illuminated by **coconut-shell oil lamps** (Chirathu).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Puppetry Traditions in Other States**:

 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**: Known for **Tholu Bommalata**, where puppets are large, multicolored, and translucent, creating vibrant shadows.
 
• **Odisha**: Known for **Ravana Chhaya**, which uses puppets made from a single piece of leather without jointed limbs, resulting in opaque, non-colored shadows.
 
• **West Bengal**: Famous for various string and rod puppetry forms like **Putul Nautch** and **Danger Putul Nach**, often performed during local fairs.
 
• **Karnataka**: Practices **Togalu Gombeyaata**, a shadow puppet form similar to those in Andhra Pradesh but with distinct regional stylistic variations.
 
• **Tamil Nadu**: Has a similar form called **Tholpavai Koothu**, which shares historical roots with the Kerala tradition but has evolved differently in its musical and linguistic execution.

questions.question: The structural and functional unit of nature is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ecosystem** is considered the **structural and functional unit of nature** because it encompasses the complex interactions between living organisms and their physical environment.
 
• The term was coined by **A.G. Tansley** in **1935** to describe a **self-regulating** and **self-sustaining** system.
 
• The **structural features** of an ecosystem consist of **biotic components** (producers, consumers, and decomposers) and **abiotic components** (temperature, light, water, and soil).
 
• The **functional aspects** of an ecosystem include **energy flow**, **nutrient cycling**, **productivity**, and **decomposition**, which ensure the continuity of life within a specific geographical area.
 
• Ecosystems can vary significantly in scale, ranging from a **small pond** or a single tree to vast **biomes** like tropical rainforests or the entire **biosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environment**:

 
 
• It refers to the **sum total** of all external conditions (physical, chemical, and biological) that surround and influence an organism.
 
• While it provides the setting for life, it lacks the specific **internal functional cycles** that define an ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Cell**:
 
 
• The **cell** is the fundamental **structural and functional unit of life** or living organisms, not of nature as a whole.
 
• All living things are composed of cells, and the study of these units is known as **Cytology**.
 
 
 
• **Ecology**:
 
 
• **Ecology** is the **scientific study** of the relationships and interactions between organisms and their environment.
 
• The concept was popularized by **Ernst Haeckel** in **1866**, who defined it as the study of the economy of nature.

questions.question: Which of the following climatic regions has permafrost soil and low vegetation like mosses and lichens?

__
 
• The **Tundra climate (ET)** is a polar climate characterized by extremely cold temperatures where the warmest month has an average temperature between **0°C** and **10°C**.
 
• The defining soil characteristic of this region is **permafrost**, which refers to ground, including rock or soil, that remains at or below **0°C** for at least **two consecutive years**.
 
• Due to the presence of **permafrost** and a very short growing season, deep-rooted trees cannot survive; instead, the landscape is dominated by low-lying vegetation such as **mosses**, **lichens**, and small **sedges**.
 
• In the **Koppen climate classification**, the **ET** designation is primarily found in the high latitudes of the **Northern Hemisphere**, covering the **Arctic** coastal fringes of North America, Eurasia, and the **Antarctic Peninsula**.
 
• The moisture levels in these regions are low, making it a **polar desert**, but the low evaporation rates allow the soil to remain moist or waterlogged during the brief summer thaw.

• Characterized by **mild winters** and cool summers with high humidity and year-round precipitation.
 
• Supports dense **temperate forests**, including both deciduous and coniferous trees, primarily in **Western Europe** and the **Pacific Northwest**.
 
 
 
• **Aw - Tropical Wet and Dry Climate**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Savanna climate**, it features a distinct **dry season** during the winter months.
 
• The vegetation consists of **tall grasses** and scattered, drought-resistant trees like the **Acacia** or **Baobab**.
 
 
 
• **BSh - Subtropical Steppe Climate**:
 
 
• A **semi-arid** climate that serves as a transition zone between desert (BW) and more humid climates.
 
• It experiences high temperatures and erratic rainfall, supporting **short-grass prairies** and xerophytic shrubs.

questions.question: What is the name of India’s first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for Sickle Cell Disease, launched in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BIRSA 101**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIRSA 101** is India’s first indigenous **CRISPR-Cas9** based gene therapy specifically designed to provide a curative treatment for **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**.
 
• Launched in **November 2025**, the therapy represents a major breakthrough in India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative in the field of advanced **biotechnology** and **genomic medicine**.
 
• The therapy was developed through a collaborative research effort led by the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** and the **Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (IGIB)**, aimed at making expensive gene treatments affordable for the Indian population.
 
• The treatment mechanism involves harvesting the patient’s own **hematopoietic stem cells**, using **CRISPR** technology to edit the **HBB gene** or induce **fetal hemoglobin (HbF)**, and then re-infusing them to produce healthy red blood cells.
 
• The naming of **BIRSA 101** pays tribute to the tribal leader **Birsa Munda**, reflecting the therapy's primary target demographic, as **Sickle Cell Disease** disproportionately affects **Scheduled Tribes** across the **tribal belt** of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**:

 
 
• It is an inherited **genetic blood disorder** where red blood cells become rigid and sickle-shaped, leading to **anemia**, **organ damage**, and **vaso-occlusive crises**.
 
• India has the second-highest global burden of **SCD**, with a high prevalence in states like **Madhya Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
 
 
• **CRISPR Technology**:
 
 
• **Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats** (CRISPR) serves as a **molecular scissor** to edit DNA with high precision.
 
• It utilizes a **guide RNA** to identify the target genetic sequence and the **Cas9 enzyme** to execute the cut, allowing for the correction of **genetic mutations**.
 
 
 
• **National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission**:
 
 
• Announced in the **Union Budget 2023-24** and launched in **July 2023**, the mission aims to eliminate the disease as a public health threat by **2047**.
 
• The mission focuses on **universal screening** of approximately 7 crore people in the age group of 0−40 years in 17 high-burden states.

questions.question: How is a country's climate performance assessed in the CCPI (Climate Change Performance Index) 2025?

options.text: Based on renewable energy production statistics only
Combining emissions, energy use and expert-reviewed climate policy data
By analyzing only national emission targets and forest cover data
Through opinion polls and industrial development trends

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combining emissions, energy use and expert-reviewed climate policy data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)** 2025 is an independent monitoring tool that evaluates the climate protection performance of **63 countries** and the **European Union**, which together account for more than **90%** of global greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The assessment framework is divided into four distinct categories with specific weightings: **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions** (40%), **Renewable Energy** (20%), **Energy Use** (20%), and **Climate Policy** (20%).
 
• The **GHG Emissions** indicator tracks current emission levels, recent trends, and the alignment of national **2030 targets** with the **Paris Agreement** goal of limiting global warming to **1.5 degrees Celsius**.
 
• The **Climate Policy** component is unique because it incorporates qualitative data through **expert-reviewed** assessments provided by approximately **450 climate and energy experts** from non-governmental organizations and think tanks.
 
• The index uses a standardized methodology to provide a comparable score for each country, determining whether their progress is **Very High**, **High**, **Medium**, **Low**, or **Very Low**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Publication and Authorship**:

 
 
• The index is published annually by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN) International**.
 
• The **CCPI 2025** report was officially released during the **COP29** summit held in **Baku, Azerbaijan**.
 
 
 
• **Methodological Limitations of Other Approaches**:
 
 
• **Renewable Energy statistics only**: This metric alone is insufficient as it does not account for the total carbon footprint or energy efficiency.
 
• **Forest Cover and National Targets**: While important for **carbon sequestration**, forest data is not a primary pillar of the CCPI, which prioritizes energy-related emissions and systemic **decarbonization**.
 
• **Opinion Polls**: Public sentiment is not a factor in the CCPI; it relies strictly on **hard data** from the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and professional policy critiques.

questions.question: The Kakori train robbery of August 1925 was organised by the:

__
 
• The **Kakori Train Robbery**, also known as the **Kakori Conspiracy**, took place on **August 9, 1925**, at **Kakori**, a village near **Lucknow** in the then **United Provinces**.
 
• The operation was orchestrated by the **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)**, a revolutionary organization founded in **October 1924** at **Kanpur** by **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**.
 
• Revolutionaries including **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Ashfaqulla Khan**, **Rajendra Lahiri**, **Chandrashekhar Azad**, and **Sachindra Bakshi** intercepted the **8-Down train** traveling from **Shahjahanpur** to **Lucknow**.
 
• The primary objective of the robbery was to seize **British government treasury** funds to purchase weaponry and finance revolutionary propaganda aimed at achieving independence through armed struggle.
 
• The incident led to the **Kakori Conspiracy Case**, resulting in the execution of **Bismil**, **Ashfaqulla Khan**, **Roshan Singh**, and **Lahiri** in **December 1927**.

• **HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association)**:

 
 
• Established in **September 1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla** in **Delhi**.
 
• It was a transformation of the **HRA** led by **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Bhagat Singh**, and **Sukhdev**, adopting **Socialist** ideals.
 
 
 
• **Ghadr Party**:
 
 
• Founded in **1913** in **San Francisco, USA**, by **Lala Hardayal** and **Sohan Singh Bhakna**.
 
• It aimed to ignite a pan-Indian revolution among Indian expatriates and soldiers to end British rule.
 
 
 
• **Anushilan Samiti**:
 
 
• A secret revolutionary society active in **Bengal** and **Bihar** during the early **20th century**.
 
• Prominent leaders included **Pramathanath Mitra**, **Aurobindo Ghosh**, and **Barindra Kumar Ghosh**, focusing on militant nationalism.
